title: Products Segre and Veronese Embeddings and Grassmannians

items.title: Products of classical algebraic sets and their universal property
items.strategy: Define X times_k Y by projections and the mapping property, distinguishing arbitrary algebraic sets (whose product may be empty) from nonempty irreducible varieties; record the point factor isomorphisms.

items.title: The product of affine varieties has coordinate ring k[X] tensor_k k[Y]
items.strategy: Use the classical affine algebraic-set/coordinate-ring duality and the tensor-product coproduct property to construct the affine algebraic set with coordinate ring k[X] tensor_k k[Y]. Over algebraically closed k use the prime-coordinate-ring criterion to prove it is a variety, then verify the classical pointwise universal property without invoking Spec or schemes at this reading order.

items.title: The Zariski topology on an affine product is generally not the product topology
items.strategy: Identify the expected fibres algebraically, then use the diagonal in A1 times A1: it is Zariski closed but is not closed for the product of the two cofinite Zariski topologies.

items.title: The Segre map from a product of projective spaces
items.strategy: Define ([x],[y]) mapsto [x_i y_j] and state its bihomogeneous coordinate convention and target projective space.

items.title: The Segre map is well defined and injective
items.strategy: Check the independent projective rescalings multiply every target coordinate by one common scalar; recover each factor from any nonzero row and column.

items.title: The Segre image is the projective rank-one locus cut out by 2 by 2 minors
items.strategy: Show products x_i y_j make all 2 by 2 minors vanish. Conversely, choose a nonzero matrix entry and factor a nonzero rank-at-most-one matrix by its row and column; conclude that the image is closed and carries the product structure.

items.title: Products of nonempty projective varieties exist as projective varieties
items.strategy: Restrict the Segre embedding to X times Y and use its rank-one closed image to obtain a projective model; verify the universal property by the ambient projective construction.

items.title: The degree-d Veronese map
items.strategy: Send a projective point to the complete list of degree-d monomials, with a fixed monomial ordering and d at least 1.

items.title: The Veronese map is a well-defined closed immersion
items.strategy: Separate the rescaling check, the standard affine-chart inverse using a nonzero pure-power coordinate, and closedness via the binomial relations among degree-d monomials.

items.title: A degree-d homogeneous equation becomes a hyperplane section under Veronese
items.strategy: Rewrite the polynomial as a linear form in the ordered degree-d monomial coordinates and pull that hyperplane back along the Veronese map.

items.title: The Grassmannian of r-dimensional subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space
items.strategy: Define Gr(r,V) as the parameter space of r-planes, including the boundary conventions Gr(0,V) and Gr(dim V,V), before giving projective coordinates.

items.title: Plucker coordinates and the Plucker map
items.strategy: For an r-plane with an ordered basis, take the projective class of its decomposable top wedge and name its basis-wedge coordinates, with the determinant change-of-basis convention.

items.title: The Plucker map is well defined and injective
items.strategy: Use the determinant action on the top wedge for basis independence; recover the subspace as the vectors whose wedge with its nonzero decomposable representative vanishes.

items.title: The Plucker image is a closed projective subvariety
items.strategy: Characterize decomposable r-vectors by the Plucker quadratic relations (equivalently rank conditions on contraction maps), proving both directions on standard nonzero-coordinate charts and hence closedness.

items.title: Standard affine charts on the Grassmannian
items.strategy: On a nonzero Plucker coordinate, put the corresponding minor in reduced row-echelon form and identify the chart with affine r times (n-r)-space; write the overlap change-of-chart argument.

items.title: The Grassmannian is smooth, irreducible, and has dimension r(n-r)
items.strategy: Use the affine chart cover for dimension and for the elementary local-affine-space sense of smoothness, and connect standard charts through their nonempty overlaps (or elementary basis changes) for irreducibility.

items.title: Incidence correspondence loci
items.strategy: Define the relevant closed-condition candidate inside a product, especially point-subspace and subspace-containment correspondences, together with its two projections.

items.title: The standard incidence locus is closed
items.strategy: Translate containment into vanishing bilinear equations in point coordinates and Plucker/minor coordinates, and invoke the closed product models already constructed.

items.title: Graphs of morphisms to a projective classical variety are closed
items.strategy: For f:X to Y in a constructed classical product X times Y, with Y projective (therefore separated in this classical setting), realize the graph as the inverse image of the closed diagonal in Y times Y; construct the diagonal from projective coordinates. State explicitly that arbitrary nonseparated prevarieties and unconstructed mixed products are excluded.

items.title: The affine diagonal is cut out by coordinate differences
items.strategy: Under k[X] tensor k[X], identify the diagonal quotient with k[X] by multiplication and present its ideal locally by x_i tensor 1 minus 1 tensor x_i.

items.title: Base change of classical varieties when the pullback exists
items.strategy: Define X times_S T by its two maps and the pullback universal property, noting the explicit affine and projective constructions available here and reserving arbitrary scheme fibre products for the later scheme treatment.

items.title: A classical fibre is base change to a point
items.strategy: For a closed k-point s of S, apply the pullback universal property to Spec(k) to identify the underlying set with f inverse(s); on affine charts, derive its defining equations by quotienting by the point ideal.

items.title: Fixed-multidegree forms define maps from products to projective space
items.strategy: For forms of one common bidegree with no common zero on the product, check independent rescaling and use the Segre coordinates to express the map locally as a projective morphism.

items.title: The Segre-Veronese map is a closed embedding
items.strategy: Compose degree-a and degree-b Veronese embeddings with the Segre embedding, and identify its bihomogeneous coordinates with all monomials of bidegree (a,b).

items.title: Why scheme fibre products are needed beyond the classical setting
items.strategy: Contrast the reduced classical affine product and point fibre with the scheme-theoretic tensor-product and quotient constructions, warning about nonreduced fibres and arbitrary base change without using later scheme results.

title: Products Segre and Veronese Embeddings and Grassmannians — Examples

items.title: The Segre image of P1 times P1 is a quadric surface
items.strategy: Write the four Segre coordinates and the single equation z00 z11 minus z01 z10 equals zero; use the rank-one theorem for the converse.

items.title: The quadratic Veronese image of P1 is a plane conic
items.strategy: Compute [s:t] mapsto [s squared:st:t squared], obtain the conic relation, and exhibit a quadratic binary form as a pulled-back line section.

items.title: Lines in P3 and the Klein quadric Gr(2,4)
items.strategy: List the six Plucker coordinates for a line in P3 and specialize the Plucker relation to the Klein quadric equation.

items.title: The boundary Grassmannians Gr(0,V) and Gr(dim V,V)
items.strategy: Verify directly that Gr(0,V) and Gr(dim V,V) each consist of one point and that the Plucker convention agrees with this description; also record that Gr(r,V) is empty when r<0 or r>dim V.

items.title: The product of Zariski topologies is too coarse on A1 times A1
items.strategy: Use the diagonal and a basic product neighbourhood to show why it cannot be closed in the product topology although it is algebraically closed.

items.title: The incidence variety of a point and a hyperplane
items.strategy: In dual projective coordinates, write the single bilinear equation sum a_i x_i equals zero and identify the two projection fibres.

items.title: Tensor products of domains need not be domains over a nonclosed field
items.strategy: Compute a concrete non-algebraically-closed-field tensor product with zero divisors and contrast it with the algebraically closed hypothesis used for affine variety products.

items.title: A bidegree (2,3) Segre-Veronese embedding
items.strategy: Enumerate the bidegree-(2,3) monomial coordinates for a small product of projective spaces and factor the map through the two Veronese maps followed by Segre.
